---
title: "Reading the files you already have"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Many files that R users have on disk are binary formats with a published layout, and the
packages that read them do it with a `readBin()` call per field. Each example below assumes
you have such a file and reads something useful out of it in a few lines: a header, an index,
or every record at once. The chunks are not run when this page is built, since they need your
files; every one was checked against a file of its format.

A header is one record: read it with `n = 1`, or `bin_unpack()` reads the layout as many
times as the bytes allow.

```{r}
library(zubin)
bits <- function(v, from, width) (v %/% 2^from) %% 2^width
```

`bits()` takes `width` bits from bit `from` of a whole number, for the formats that pack
fields narrower than a byte.

## An SQLite database

The first 100 bytes of every SQLite file are a big-endian header: the page size, the page
count, the text encoding and the version of SQLite that last wrote it, read without opening
the database.

```{r}
x <- readBin("data.sqlite", "raw", 100)
h <- bin_unpack(x, ">magic:s16 page_size:u16 write:u8 read:u8 x4 changes:u32 pages:u32 x8
                   schema:u32 format:u32 x8 encoding:u32 user_version:u32 x4 app_id:u32
                   x20 valid_for:u32 sqlite:u32")
h$size <- h$pages * ifelse(h$page_size == 1, 65536, h$page_size)
h$encoding <- c("UTF-8", "UTF-16le", "UTF-16be")[h$encoding]
h$sqlite <- sprintf("%d.%d.%d", h$sqlite %/% 1e6, h$sqlite %/% 1e3 %% 1e3, h$sqlite %% 1e3)
h[c("magic", "page_size", "pages", "size", "encoding", "sqlite")]
```

## An ESRI shapefile of points

A `.shp` header mixes byte orders in one record: the file code and length are big-endian, the
version, shape type and bounding box little-endian. A file of points has records of one size,
28 bytes, so every point is one call after the header.

```{r}
x <- readBin("stations.shp", "raw", file.size("stations.shp"))
h <- bin_unpack(x, ">code:i32 x20 words:i32 version:i32.le type:i32.le
                   xmin:f64.le ymin:f64.le xmax:f64.le ymax:f64.le x32", n = 1)
stopifnot(h$code == 9994, h$type == 1)          # 1: Point
pts <- bin_unpack(x, ">id:i32 words:i32 type:i32.le x:f64.le y:f64.le", offset = 100)
head(pts[c("id", "x", "y")])
```

## Geometries from sf, as well-known binary

`sf::st_as_binary()` gives each geometry as WKB: a byte for the byte order, a `u32`
geometry type, then the coordinates. For points, each one is 21 bytes, and the whole column
reads in one call:

```{r}
wkb <- sf::st_as_binary(sf::st_geometry(stations))
x <- do.call(c, unclass(wkb))
p <- bin_unpack(x, "<order:u8 type:u32 x:f64 y:f64")
stopifnot(all(p$order == 1), all(p$type == 1))  # little-endian points
head(p[c("x", "y")])
```

## PLINK genotypes

A PLINK `.bed` file is a 3-byte magic number and then, for each variant, the genotypes of
all samples at 2 bits each, four to a byte, low bits first. `00` is two copies of the first
allele, `01` missing, `10` one copy, `11` none. The sample and variant counts are the line
counts of the `.fam` and `.bim` files beside it.

```{r}
n <- length(readLines("study.fam"))
x <- readBin("study.bed", "raw", file.size("study.bed"))
stopifnot(identical(x[1:3], as.raw(c(0x6c, 0x1b, 0x01))))  # variant-major
b <- bin_decode(x, "u8", offset = 3)
codes <- outer(c(0, 2, 4, 6), b, function(at, v) bits(v, at, 2))
g <- matrix(c(2, NA, 1, 0)[codes + 1], nrow = 4 * ceiling(n / 4))[seq_len(n), ]
dim(g)                                          # samples by variants
```

## An EEG or sleep recording (EDF)

An EDF header is ASCII in fixed-width fields: 256 bytes for the recording, then each field
of the signal table for every signal in turn. Reading a field for all signals is one call with
`n`, and the samples are little-endian `i16`.

```{r}
x <- readBin("sleep.edf", "raw", file.size("sleep.edf"))
h <- bin_unpack(x, "version:s8 patient:s80 recording:s80 date:s8 time:s8 bytes:s8 x44
                   records:s8 duration:s8 signals:s4", n = 1)
ns <- as.integer(h$signals)
label <- trimws(bin_unpack(x, "label:s16", offset = 256, n = ns)$label)
spr <- as.integer(bin_unpack(x, "n:s8", offset = 256 + 216 * ns, n = ns)$n)
first <- bin_decode(x, "i16", offset = as.integer(h$bytes), n = spr[1])  # signal 1, record 1
```

## A genome in UCSC `.2bit`

A `.2bit` file holds a 16-byte header, an index of sequence names and offsets, and the
sequences at 2 bits per base. The index alone gives every sequence's name and length:

```{r}
x <- readBin("genome.2bit", "raw", 1e6)  # enough for the index; see below
h <- bin_unpack(x, "<sig:u32 version:u32 count:u32 x4", n = 1)
stopifnot(h$sig == 0x1A412743)
at <- 16; seqs <- NULL
for (i in seq_len(h$count)) {
  len <- bin_decode(x, "u8", offset = at, n = 1)
  e <- bin_unpack(x, sprintf("name:s%d offset:u32", len), offset = at + 1, n = 1)
  seqs <- rbind(seqs, e); at <- at + 1 + len + 4
}
```

Each sequence's length is the `u32` at its offset, most of them far into the file: `seek()` a
connection to each one rather than reading the whole genome.

## An SPSS data file

A `.sav` file opens with a 176-byte header in the byte order of the machine that wrote it.
The format stores the number 100 as a double, the *bias*, and readers decode the header both
ways and keep the one in which the bias is 100:

```{r}
x <- readBin("survey.sav", "raw", 176)
spec <- "magic:s4 product:s60 layout:i32 case_size:i32 compressed:i32 weight:i32 cases:i32
         bias:f64 date:s9 time:s8 label:s64 x3"
h <- bin_unpack(x, paste("<", spec))
if (h$bias != 100) h <- bin_unpack(x, paste(">", spec))
h[c("product", "cases", "date", "time", "label")]
```

## R's own files

An `.rds` file is gzip-compressed by default; `gzfile()` reads through that, and the header
says which version of R wrote the file and which one it needs:

```{r}
con <- gzfile("model.rds", "rb"); x <- readBin(con, "raw", 64); close(con)
h <- bin_unpack(x, ">magic:s2 format:i32 writer:u32 reader:u32 enc_len:i32", n = 1)
ver <- function(v) sprintf("%d.%d.%d", v %/% 65536, v %/% 256 %% 256, v %% 256)
c(written_by = ver(h$writer), readable_from = ver(h$reader),
  encoding = rawToChar(x[19 + seq_len(h$enc_len) - 1]))
```

## A Parquet file's footer

A Parquet file ends with the length of its metadata, a little-endian `u32`, and the magic
`PAR1`. The metadata itself is Thrift-encoded, which zubin does not decode, but its size and
position are where every Parquet reader starts:

```{r}
size <- file.size("sales.parquet")
con <- file("sales.parquet", "rb"); invisible(seek(con, size - 8))
x <- readBin(con, "raw", 8); close(con)
f <- bin_unpack(x, "<length:u32 magic:s4")
stopifnot(f$magic == "PAR1")
c(metadata_bytes = f$length, metadata_at = size - 8 - f$length)
```
